$comment: APPROVED, NAMED, EXPIRING suppressions for the integration shard.
A test that appears here is still counted against the full EXPECTED population. It is not removed
from the denominator, because reducing the denominator by the tests you expect to skip encodes the
suppression into the success criterion: the gate then passes forever while those tests never run.
Every suppression this project has found was justified when it was written, and every one survived
for the same structural reason -- doing nothing preserved it. So neglect must REMOVE a suppression,
* expires, id and owner are MANDATORY. An entry missing any of them fails the gate, so the
* a PAST expiry is a REFUSE, not a warning. The suppression stops working and the build stops.
* renewal requires FRESH EVIDENCE, not a fresh date. Bumping the date is the failure mode that
would defeat the whole mechanism, because it makes an unreviewed entry LOOK reviewed. Record a
new measurement in evidence: what was run, on what, and what it showed.
* the list may only SHRINK. Growth is a reviewable diff with a named approver, never a runtime
The gate prints this file in full on every run, with days remaining. Suppressions become invisible

REFERENCE DIRECTION. This file is mirrored and world-visible, so it carries NO internal tracker id. The tracking issue names this entry by its 'id'; this entry never names the issue. Internal artifacts may point at public ones, never the reverse -- a public file that cites an internal work item leaks it and means nothing to the consumer reading it.
by going unread; this is the one moment someone is looking.

entries.reason: All 15 facts call SkipIfVaultUnavailable(), which is Assert.SkipWhen(_provider is null, "AZURE_KEYVAULT_URI environment variable not set"). The variable is never set in CI, so the provider is always null and every fact skips. Unlike Cosmos DB there is no Azure Key Vault emulator, so this cannot be closed by adding a container: it needs a real Key Vault resource and credentials in the CI environment.
entries.evidence: Measured 2026-08-01 on the committed tree. The class declares 15 [Fact] and 0 [Theory]; all 15 route through SkipIfVaultUnavailable() at AzureKeyVaultProviderIntegrationShould.cs:332. AZURE_KEYVAULT_URI appears exactly once in the workflow tree, at ci.yml:655, inside a step whose own comment reads 'These are DIAGNOSTIC PRINTS, not probes... they cannot fail' -- it reports whether the variable is set and never sets it. No workflow assigns it and no secret is bound to it. So the skip is not intermittent and not environmental drift: it is the guaranteed outcome of every run on the current configuration, and has been for as long as the variable has been unset. What is NOT established: whether these 15 facts pass against a real Key Vault. They have not been observed running anywhere, so this entry records untested coverage, not passing coverage.

entries.reason: Every arm skips because the Elasticsearch container was not reachable from InitializeAsync. Unlike the sibling Azure Blob suite, whose skip turned out to be an API-version rejection by a running container, this one appears to be genuine absence.
entries.evidence: Measured 2026-08-02 on the CI integration shard. The skip reports '[infrastructure-unavailable] Elasticsearch (Docker) was not reachable from InitializeAsync'. Corroborated independently by the coverage artifact from the SAME run: MonitoredResilientElasticsearchClient is 0.0% covered, 0 of 614 lines, across all four result files -- so no arm executed anywhere in the shard, not merely in this class. The contrast is the point: Azure Blob's cold store read 85.0% covered while its own suite skipped, which is how that skip was exposed as a false claim of absence. RENEWED 2026-10-02, and one of the two open questions is now CLOSED: all 8 arms PASS against a reachable Elasticsearch, 0 skipped, measured locally on Docker in 5 seconds. So the arms are sound and the skip is purely about reachability in CI's environment. STILL NOT established: WHY the container is unreachable there. This renewal is deliberately short because the remaining question is a CI-environment defect that an allowlist cannot fix, only postpone.

entries.reason: ThrowNotNoOpOnPersistenceFailure has to break the backing store to assert anything, and the fault cannot be induced against the Firestore emulator: the .NET client runs as emulator admin and bypasses security rules by construction, Firestore exposes no rename or permission-revoke primitive at collection or document level, and stopping and restarting the container did not return a reachable gRPC channel inside a workable test timeout. This is a SUPPRESSION and not a structural exemption: the inbox store plainly exposes a persistence surface, so the cause is fixable and the entry is renewable rather than permanent. Its 34 sibling arms in the same class are unaffected and run, which is why count is 1.
entries.evidence: Measured 2026-10-11 on the nightly excalibur integration shard, run 38131952682 job 114449193076: 3936 passed, 1 NotExecuted, and the lane refused although every test that ran passed. Three independent checks require every required test to be Passed, each verified by running it against that run's own downloaded TRX -- the per-test outcome requirement in required-test-evidence.py, and in validate-shard-results.ps1 both the diagnostic allowlist and the total-equals-executed-equals-passed counter check. The arm is now excluded from the nightly population by a per-test RequiresFaultInjection category, verified surgical: discovery over the project returned 3857 tests without the term and 3856 with it, the one test in the difference being the intended arm. WHAT THIS ENTRY IS FOR, since the exclusion means it approves no skip today: a filter term carries no owner and no expiry, so without this entry neglect would preserve the gap silently and forever. The expiry here is enforced per-entry on every CI run independently of whether the test was observed skipping, so this date is what forces the question back. NOT established: whether the arm passes against a real durability fault. It has never been observed running, so this records untested coverage rather than passing coverage, and the guarantee contract records it as UNVERIFIED. Renewal requires a new measurement, not a new date: the next approach is a severable TCP proxy in front of the emulator container, which changes how every Firestore inbox test connects and is therefore its own careful pass.
